  whether you stole one, not its kind; they are told which kind they lost. If they have no tokens, nothing
  happens and they aren't told. A steal from a player who dies that night still takes the token and counts (R10).
  Win: iff you steal tokens from 3 different players (a second steal from the same player takes nothing). If you
  are alive then, the moderator reveals you at once and you leave the game (as for the Executioner). If you died
  that night, you still win and nothing is revealed.

Vulture
  Win: alone, if you are alive at the start of a Day (after the night's deaths) and your threshold or fewer players
  are alive, counting yourself. The game then ends at once and everyone else loses (wins already earned by roles
  that never block wins still count, R1). Your threshold starts at 2.
  Night: may visit another player. If they die that night (by any cause, end-of-night effects included), you are
  told at the end of the night that they died and their role (exact-role check, R19; nothing more if a Mortician
  cleaned them), and you get the first of these power-ups you don't have yet: +1 to your threshold, Standard
  Defense, +1 to your threshold, Strong Defense, then +1 to your threshold for each later one. Your threshold
  never goes above max(floor(N/3), 2), where N is the number of players at the start of the game; a power-up that
  would raise it further is skipped. If they don't die, nothing happens and you are told so.

Decoy
  Never blocks wins (R1).
  Win: iff you die at night. You lose if you die by Day or the game ends with you alive.
  If an attack killed you at night, the next Day's announcements say you were the Decoy and name 3 players: every
  player whose attack would have killed you on its own (3 of them at random if there were more), then random other
  players alive at the start of that Day to make 3 (fewer if not enough are left). The names are in random order,
  and the announcement doesn't say how many of them attacked you. Your cause of death and last will show as usual.

=== PART 7: TRAITS ===

R24 (Traits)
Some players also have a trait: an extra ability on top of their role. You are told your own trait at the start
(except a hidden trait, which says so); nobody else is told, not even your teammates, and whether a game has any
traits is secret. Investigations never see traits: they report roles and alignments only. A trait stays with you if
your role changes. Traits are always true: a Roleplayer's trait is real even though its role isn't. A player may
have more than one trait, but never the same one twice. Each trait below says who can get it (Who), whether it is
hidden from its holder (Hidden), whether at most one player in a game has it (Unique), what it does (Effect) and
which traits nobody holds together with it (Never with). A trait's night action is used in addition to your role's
own, and a role-block stops it too.

--- Village players only ---

Martyr
  Who: Village players only.
  Effect: If you are hanged, the announcement of your death also says you were a Martyr and names every player whose
  vote counted as Guilty in your trial. Your role stays hidden. A Martyr who dies any other way shows nothing.

Cursed
  Who: Village players only.
  Effect: If you die, a random living Good player (if any) is dealt a Divine Attack at the end of the night: the
  night you died, or the night after the Day you died. It comes after all of that night's other actions and attacks,
  so the victim is drawn from the Good players still alive then, and it counts as a death that night. Its cause is
  "a curse". It needs no action, so a role-block doesn't stop it.

Avenger
  Who: Village players only.
  Effect: If you are killed at night, every player whose attack would have killed you is dealt a Basic Attack (an
  Astral Visit) that same night. Defense and protection apply as usual (R3); a kill's cause is "Avenger". Attacks
  that weren't fatal on their own, and deaths by Day, set nothing off. It needs no action, so a role-block doesn't
  stop it.

Kindred
  Who: Village players only.
  Effect: After each trial vote you cast, you privately learn up to two random other players whose votes counted the
  same way as the vote you cast (if fewer did, you learn that). It needs no action, so a role-block doesn't stop it.

Remorseful
  Who: Village players only.
  Effect: If you vote Guilty in a trial and that player is hanged and was Village (their true alignment), you die at
  once; the cause is "remorse". It goes by the vote you cast. It isn't an attack, so nothing that reacts to attacks
  counts it.
  Never with: Zealot.

Ashamed
  Who: Village players only.
  Effect: If you vote Innocent in a trial and that player is hanged and wasn't Village (their true alignment: Yakuza
  or Neutral), you die at once; the cause is "shame". It goes by the vote you cast. It isn't an attack, so nothing
  that reacts to attacks counts it.
  Never with: Merciful or Turncoat.

Faultline
  Who: Village players only.
  Effect: After each trial vote you cast, you privately learn one random other player whose vote counted as Guilty
  and one whose vote counted as Innocent (if all the others voted one way, you learn that). It needs no action, so a
  role-block doesn't stop it.

Notorious
  Who: Village players only.
  Effect: Alignment checks see you as Evil (R19). Checks that see true alignment, such as the Census Taker's count,
  aren't fooled.
  Never with: Turncoat.

Stolen Blade
  Who: Village players only.
  Effect: Once per game, at night, you may attack another living player with a stolen Katana: a Standard Attack,
  besides your role's own action. It is an action and a visit by you, and it looks exactly like the Yakuza's Katana
  attack: a kill's cause is "Katana", and a surviving target learns only that they were attacked with the Katana.
  You learn only whether it killed. A role-block stops it, and then it isn't used up.
  Never with: Armed.

Paranoid
  Who: Village players only.
  Hidden: you aren't told you have this trait.
  Effect: On each night, with probability 1/4, you are told you were attacked and survived, though nobody attacked
  you. The made-up attack is the Katana's 2/3 of the time, and otherwise a Vigilante's or a Serial Killer's (always
  the Katana's when neither role can be in the game); it is worded like a real one. Nothing else happens: it isn't a
  visit or an attack, and nobody else learns of it.
  Never with: Oblivious.

Turncoat
  Who: Village players only.
  Unique: at most one player in a game has it.
  Effect: You win only if the Yakuza win (alive or dead), and you lose otherwise, even if the Village wins.
  Alignment checks see you as Evil (R19); checks that see true alignment, such as the Census Taker's count, see you
  as Good. You stay Village in every other way: you aren't in the Yakuza's chat or Katana votes, you don't know who
  the Yakuza are, and they aren't told about you. The game's end ignores you, like a role that never blocks wins
  (R1): it ends when the other living players are all Village or all Yakuza.
  Never with: Ashamed, Notorious, Rival, Selfish, Selfless or Spiteful.

Spiteful
  Who: Village players only, except a Saint.
  Unique: at most one player in a game has it.
  Effect: If you are hanged, from then on you win only if the Yakuza win (alive or dead), and you lose otherwise,
  even if the Village wins. Until then you win with the Village as usual, and dying any other way changes nothing.
  Nobody is told you switched, and your will is revealed as usual.
  Never with: Rival, Selfish, Selfless or Turncoat.

--- Yakuza players only ---

Spare Blade
  Who: Yakuza players only.
  Effect: Once per game, at night, you may make one extra Katana attack on another living player, whoever holds the
  Katana and besides its own attack (which the Yakuza still choose as usual, R8). It is Standard, an action and a
  visit by you, and its target learns only that they were attacked with the Katana. A role-block stops it, and then
  it isn't used up.
  Never with: Armed or Berserker.

Usurper
  Who: Yakuza players only.
  Unique: at most one player in a game has it.
  Effect: You win only if the Yakuza win while you are the only Yakuza alive, and then you take the win alone: the
  other Yakuza, alive or dead, don't win. If the Yakuza win with another Yakuza alive, they win and you don't. Your
  teammates aren't told.
  Never with: Selfish or Selfless.

Shaky
  Who: Yakuza players only.
  Hidden: you aren't told you have this trait.
  Effect: Every Katana attack you make (the Katana's own while you hold it, or a Spare Blade attack) is level None,
  so it never kills (R3); it is still an attack and a visit.
  Never with: Berserker, Katana Expert or Katana Master.

Katana Expert
  Who: Yakuza players only.
  Effect: Once per game, on a night you hold the Katana, you may make its own attack Strong instead of Standard.
  Choose it with your night action and name the player the Katana attacks; it works only if you hold the Katana at
  the end of that night and it attacks that player, and only then is it used up. A role-block on you stops it along
  with the attack, and it isn't used up.
  Never with: Berserker, Katana Master or Shaky.

Katana Master
  Who: Yakuza players only.
  Effect: Like Katana Expert, but the attack is Divine, which no Defense, protection, trap or charm stops.
  Never with: Berserker, Katana Expert or Shaky.

Berserker
  Who: Yakuza players only.
  Effect: Once per game, on a night you hold the Katana, you may make its attack rampage: besides its own attack, it
  makes a Standard Katana attack on every other player who visits its target that night, whatever their faction.
  These attacks on visitors aren't visits, and Astral Visits aren't visits, so their makers aren't attacked. Choose it
  with your night action and name the player the Katana attacks; it works only if you hold the Katana at the end of
  that night and it attacks that player, and only then is it used up. A role-block on you stops it along with the
  attack, and it isn't used up. Each attacked player learns only that they were attacked with the Katana; you learn
  how many players the rampage attacked and how many of those attacks killed, not who the visitors were.
  Never with: Katana Expert, Katana Master, Shaky or Spare Blade.

--- Village and Yakuza players only ---

Armed
  Who: Village and Yakuza players only.
  Effect: Once per game, at night, you may fire a hidden gun at another living player: a Basic Attack. It is an
  action and a visit, and a role-blocked shot isn't used up. You learn only whether it killed its target. A kill's
  cause is "a hidden gun".
  Never with: Spare Blade or Stolen Blade.

Bonded
  Who: Village and Yakuza players only.
  Effect: You and one other random Village or Yakuza player are bonded, and each of you is told the other's name
  (not their role or faction). If either of you dies, the other dies of heartbreak at once (its cause is
  "heartbreak"). Heartbreak isn't an attack, so nothing that reacts to attacks counts it.
  Never with: Rival.

Rival
  Who: Village and Yakuza players only.
  Effect: You and one other random player of your own faction are rivals, and each of you is told the other's name
  (not their role). Each of you wins only if your faction wins and the other has died by the end; whether you are
  alive doesn't matter. Your faction's win doesn't change.
  Never with: Bonded, Spiteful or Turncoat.

Selfish
  Who: Village and Yakuza players only.
  Effect: You win only if your faction wins and you are alive at the end. Your faction's win doesn't change; you
  just don't share it if you died.
  Never with: Selfless, Spiteful, Turncoat or Usurper.

Selfless
  Who: Village and Yakuza players only.
  Effect: You win only if your faction wins and you are dead at the end. Your faction's win doesn't change; you just
  don't share it if you're alive.
  Never with: Selfish, Spiteful, Turncoat or Usurper.

--- Any player ---

Grudge
  Who: Any player.
  Effect: If you are hanged, the next night one random player whose vote counted as Guilty in your trial, among
  those alive when that night begins, is dealt a Standard Attack (an Astral Visit). Defense and protection apply as
  usual. A kill's cause is "a grudge". It needs no action, so a role-block doesn't stop it.

Loud
  Who: Any player.
  Effect: You earn 1.5 times the usual speaking budget each round, and your cap is 1.5 times the usual (R22). Your
  prices and trial-only budget are the usual ones.

Curt
  Who: Any player.
  Effect: The length part of your message prices (R22) is doubled, so long messages cost you much more; each
  message's base fee, nominations and your trial-only budget are the usual ones.

Confidant
  Who: Any player.
  Effect: Once per game, on one of your own Day turns, you may send one private message hidden: nobody else is told
  it was sent, and the public ledger doesn't count it. Its recipient sees that it was hidden. Players who hear
  private messages (e.g. the Wiretap) still hear it, also marked hidden.

Zealot
  Who: Any player whose role doesn't change how much their own trial vote counts.
  Effect: Every Guilty/Innocent trial vote you cast counts as Guilty, whatever you vote, including in your own
  trial. Your nomination (Yes/No) votes are unchanged. Your private reminder shows both the vote you cast and how it
  counted, and everything that reports how you voted (e.g. the Auditor, a Martyr's announcement) uses the vote as
  counted. A Fixer's reversal doesn't change it.
  Never with: Merciful or Remorseful.

Merciful
  Who: Any player whose role doesn't change how much their own trial vote counts.
  Effect: Like Zealot, but your trial votes always count as Innocent.
  Never with: Ashamed or Zealot.

Drowsy
  Who: Any player whose role has a night action and can be role-blocked.
  Hidden: you aren't told you have this trait.
  Effect: On each night, with probability 1/2, you are role-blocked (R9) with no blocker. On those nights you are
  told you were role-blocked, as with any role-block.

Stocked
  Who: Any player whose role starts with tokens and can ever have more than it starts with.
  Effect: You start with one more of each kind of token your role starts with.

Disguised
  Who: Any player.
  Effect: You are told a Village role (never your own), drawn at the start. Every exact-role check (R18) sees you as
  that role instead of yours, alive or dead; alignment checks still see your true alignment.

Narrow Escape
  Who: Any player.
  Hidden: you aren't told you have this trait.
  Effect: Once per game, on the first night an attack that isn't Divine would kill you (after Defense, protection,
  traps and charms), you survive: every non-Divine attack on you that night fails instead. It works like Strong
  Defense on every night until then, so a night when nothing would have killed you (e.g. a Medic stopped the attack)
  doesn't use it up. Divine Attacks and deaths by Day aren't stopped. You are told about the failed attacks as for
  any others (R3).

Oblivious
  Who: Any player.
  Hidden: you aren't told you have this trait.
  Effect: You are never told about an attack you survive.
  Never with: Paranoid.

Sleepwalker
  Who: Any player.
  Effect: Every night you visit one random other living player, besides any action of your own; code draws it, and
  you aren't told whom. It does nothing but visit: anything that sees or reacts to visits (R6), such as a Tracker, a
  Lookout or a Veteran's alert, counts it. It isn't optional, but a role-block stops it (R7).

---

answers.bugs_or_oddities: The Night 2 Scout result said there were 2 visit groups. From the public visits there should have been at least three or four: Alice alone, Bob alone (he visited no one), Carol/Heidi/Frank, and Grace/Erin linked by my Night 2 protection. The Night 4 result said Alice, Carol and Grace were in separate groups, but Grace visited Alice, so they must have been linked. Both results conflict with visits in the public record. Either the Scout was a Roleplayer (the final reveal confirms Alice was one), or the group calculation leaves out protection visits.
answers.suggestions: 1) Mark Roleplayer results somehow, or state in the rules that exact-role and group claims can be false without the claimant being Yakuza. Alternatively, announce the number of Roleplayers at game start. 2) State explicitly whether protections and astral visits count as links in group results. 3) Tell Medics whether their protected target was attacked at all, not only whether the protection stopped it. 4) When a Scout's group result contradicts public visits, say so. 5) Offer a cheap private way to ask the moderator to verify a claim's role.

answers.confusing_rules:
The Roleplayer rules were hard to use in practice. A Roleplayer is told a role and gets random results, and the rules say those results are true only by chance. Nobody at the table could tell which claimants were Roleplayers, so every mechanical check I made on Days 3-5 may have been meaningless. Three of the four claimants (Dave, Erin, Alice) turned out to be Roleplayers in the final reveal. I didn't realize the design allowed this until the end, and I had no way to weigh it during play.

The timing of last wills around a night death is also unclear. A will is written at the start of Night. Night results arrive at the same moment as the death, so a player who dies at night can't add those results. It's not clear whether they can update the will after results and before the death is announced.
answers.missing_information:
I couldn't tell which players were Roleplayers, so I couldn't judge how reliable any claim's result was. The public ledger listed claims but not which claims were reliable.

I never saw my speaking budget after Day 2, because I died before Day 3's budget mattered to me. I'm not sure whether the budget carried over correctly from Day 2 to Day 3. I'd like the remaining budget shown with each turn, as it was on Day 2.

The Night 2 visit groups were hard to check against the visits the public could see. Heidi visited Frank, Carol visited Heidi, and Grace visited Erin. Those links alone make at least three groups, but Alice's public Scout result said there were two.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt:
I wanted to post my Night 2 Sheriff result (Frank read Evil) before I died. The result arrived in the same moment as my death, so I had no Day turn to post it, and my last will (written at Night start) didn't include it. A prompt to update the will right after the night results, before the death is revealed, would have let me publish it.

I also wanted to test Frank on Day 2 through a vote, but that was just a choice I made. The interface didn't block anything for me.
answers.bugs_or_oddities:
1. Night 2 Scout groups: Alice was told "only 2 visit groups: Alice and Heidi." The visits I could see (Carol -> Heidi, Heidi -> Frank, Grace -> Erin) make at least three groups. This is consistent with Alice being a Roleplayer, whose results are random, but the table had no way to see that.

2. Night 4 Scout groups: Carol's Katana attack on Grace is a visit, so Carol and Grace should be in one group. Alice's public result put them in separate groups. Same explanation as above.

3. Frank's Night 2 read was Evil on my Sheriff check. Erin's Coroner exam said Frank was a Hitman, and the rules say Killing Neutrals read Not Evil. The Evil read fits Frank being a Yakuza Grunt (he was in the Yakuza night chat), so the Hitman exam is the inconsistent part. Erin was a Roleplayer, so the exam was random.

4. Dave's Profiler result on Frank said Frank was a Census Taker, Magpie or Medic, with exactly one true. Frank's real role was Grunt, so the "exactly one is true" promise did not hold for this result. Again the cause is the Roleplayer mechanic, but a Profiler's stated guarantee is violated, which is confusing.

5. Dead players' Roleplayer results were posted as if they were real exact-role checks (Erin's Trapper, Hitman and Profiler exams), so the same unverified claim source produced a lot of confident-sounding information.
answers.suggestions:
1. Tell the table at the start, in a neutral way, that some claimed roles may be Roleplayers (or that Roleplayer results are random) without saying who. That would make claim-checking more honest.

2. Let a player who dies at night add a final will update after their night results arrive and before the death is revealed. Right now their last information is lost.

3. Show the remaining speaking budget with each turn prompt, and say whether it carries over from Day 2 to Day 3.

4. Consider stating at the end of the night, to the affected players, that a visit or result came from a random source. That would give honest players a way to notice inconsistent results.

answers.confusing_rules:
1) The Roleplayer's imaginary tokens. The rules say the Roleplayer's actions "only happen in your imagination" and its results are random. They don't say whether it gets the told role's tokens, or whether those tokens go down as it uses them. I decided it does: I reported "2 profile tokens left" to Dave and counted Erin's coroner tokens down 3→2→1→0. I also applied the told role's targeting limits: Erin as Coroner had no valid target on Night 1, and could only examine players who were already dead. None of this is written down.
2) What a random Roleplayer result can be. "Drawn at random from the results your role could get that night" doesn't say which pool of roles to use for a Coroner or Profiler result. It could be every role in the rules except Vanilla Villager (the setup excludes it), or only roles that fit the setup. My fake results named Trapper, Hitman, Profiler, Census Taker, Magpie and Medic. I also had to decide whether a fake Coroner result could be "cleaned by Mortician". I also didn't know whether unique roles (Hitman) still count as unique inside fake results.
3) The "never contradicts a public, true announcement" rule only covers roles and alignments. Public facts about deaths limit Scout and Cartographer results too. A Katana death means the victim had a visitor, so the victim can't be in a group of 1. Alice's Night 4 result put Grace in a different group from Alice and Carol, while Grace died to the Katana. It was technically allowed, but only because Erin could fill Grace's group. I wasn't sure whether such results have to fit the public death record.
4) Scout output when there are 1 or 2 groups. I had to choose the wording ("only 2 visit groups; one from each", "all in one visit group, including Carol").
answers.missing_information: There was no tool to work out the real visit groups (Cartographer/Scout) or to check a Roleplayer's fake result against public facts. I did it by hand. There was no state panel for Roleplayer imaginary tokens, real tokens, or who was a valid target (dead before the night versus dying tonight). There was no record of which fake result I had already given each Roleplayer, which would help keep fakes plausible from night to night. There was also no quick view of the circle order after deaths, to check speaking order.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: I wanted to generate Roleplayer results with a tool, so they come from a defined distribution instead of my own picks. I also wanted to flag a player misreading the rules out of game. Both Yakuza openly claimed "Grunt" as cover, and the Village treated it as a Yakuza confession. Frank still survived to Day 3, and nobody pointed out that a Yakuza claim should normally be lethal. As moderator I had no channel to raise this, and possibly shouldn't have one.
answers.bugs_or_oddities:
1) The Night 4 action log lists "Carol (Grunt): target Grace". Every other night lists "no role action" plus the Katana vote. The Katana target ended up recorded as a role-action target, so the log format is inconsistent.
2) The Yakuza planned "Grunt with no night action" as their *cover*. It looks like the "(Grunt)" label in the Yakuza night summary made them think Grunt was a safe public claim.
3) This hand-picked setup gave 3 of the 6 Village players the Roleplayer role. Combined with 2 Yakuza in an 8-player game, the Village was flooded with false information. Erin's fake Coroner exams and Alice's fake Scout groups directly led to the town hanging Bob and then Erin. This was all within the rules, but it's very lopsided.
4) Day 2 ran all 8 rounds of nearly identical "no nomination from me, Frank give one concrete detail" messages. The speaking budget didn't discourage this.
5) The mechanics I checked held up: nomination thresholds, kills, the Medic stop on Night 3, Heidi's Night 2 result not reaching her will, and the game ending after Night 5.
answers.suggestions:
- Spell out how a Roleplayer's tokens and targeting limits work: they mirror the told role's, imaginary but counted down.
- Define the pool that fake results draw from.
- Extend "never contradicts" to public death facts that limit visit-based results, or say explicitly that it doesn't.
- Give the moderator a tool that computes visit groups, plus a seeded generator for Roleplayer results.
- Make the action log format the same when a Yakuza Grunt holds the Katana.
- Cap how many copies of Roleplayer a hand-picked setup can have, or warn when Outsiders are a large share of the Village.
- Remind Yakuza players privately that Yakuza role names are self-incriminating claims.
- Make repeated near-identical public messages cost more, so stalled Days end sooner.

title: Post-game lessons: tips players wish they'd known, and how past tips went

task:
If you played this game again, what tips and tricks do you wish you'd known? Give 1-5 concrete, reusable lessons (not a recap of this game), each with a topic and who it applies to (a role, a faction, or 'everyone').

You were also given tips from past games (in your instructions). Which of them went especially well or badly for you or others this game? List only tips that clearly mattered (or none): helped, hurt (followed it and it backfired, or it was predictable to opponents), or wrong (it is false or contradicts the rules), and why, concretely.

lessons.applies_to: Village power roles holding kill tokens (Vigilante, Sniper, Enforcer)
lessons.tip: Don't hold kill tokens for a perfect break. Once the Katana has killed several players and the Village is down to about five, the Katana holder keeps acting every night. Fire on the best suspect you have while you still have several living Village players to back the shot, because a dead Vigilante with unused tokens has zero effect.

Scout and group results are the strongest mechanical evidence in the game, so check every claimed visit against them. A Medic's protection, a Sheriff check or a Coroner exam all imply a visit. If a claimed visit puts two players in different groups, one of the two claims is false. Work out which before anyone is hanged.

Don't hang on a 'concrete break' that is only an unverified claim about a visit. Two Village-aligned players were hanged on arguments that later proved wrong, and the Yakuza-side player kept pushing the same trial. Demand a result that a public exact-role check or a group size can confirm before the vote.

Keep the Katana holder's cover consistent and avoid pushing hard in the same trials as your partner. Carol stayed quiet, voted with the Village, and never revealed a night role, and that let the Katana holder survive to the end. Drop the Katana holder's cover claim only when a kill would otherwise leave the Yakuza with no living member.

A false exact-role claim like 'Grunt' is easy to break with a Coroner exam. Pick a cover whose role an exam can't contradict, such as a Village role with no night action, and don't name a Yakuza-side role publicly.

tips_feedback.tip: Before voting Guilty, name a concrete mechanical break, and vote on mechanical evidence.
tips_feedback.why: The Village voted Guilty on group arithmetic that depended on claimed visits. The arithmetic was often incomplete, and it hanged a Good Coroner-adjacent read and a Good Vigilante. The tip was followed, but the breaks were not verified, so the Yakuza-side players could use the same logic against the Village.

tips_feedback.tip: Spend one-shot tokens at the first night or Day they can change a vote, because they die with you.
tips_feedback.why: I held three shot tokens and never fired them. Because of this tip I waited for a confirmed break that never came, so the tokens were wasted when I was executed. Waiting did not protect them, and firing on the best suspect earlier might have changed the outcome.

tips_feedback.tip: Treat a lone visitor to a Katana victim as near-proof only when a second source corroborates it.
tips_feedback.why: The Scout's group read on Night 3 and Grace's protection were the two sources that matched, and the Village used that match to rule out Carol and Erin. The rule kept the Village from trusting a single unverified claim, though the Scout read on Night 4 later contradicted Grace's will.

tips_feedback.tip: Answer a direct question about your night action in one plain sentence the first time it is asked.
tips_feedback.why: Bob and Frank gave plain answers when pressed, and the Village could then test them against the Scout groups. The dodgers were the ones pushed out first.

lessons.tip: A Roleplayer can post a confident exact-role or Coroner exam that is simply false, since its results are random. Before a hang rests on one exam, check it against a second independent source, such as a Scout group or a visit someone can actually confirm. Don't let one exam overrule a claimed role that fits the voting pattern. Here, Erin's exams cleared Frank, who was really a Yakuza Grunt, and convicted Bob, who was a real Village Vigilante.

Watch which power claimants the Katana kills. Night 1 and Night 2 kills hit Dave, then Heidi, the Sheriff claimant. Later the Yakuza hit Grace, the Medic, and Alice, the Scout. A claimant the Katana kills is probably real and was a threat to the Yakuza. Treat the claims that survive as a set, and check which ones the kill order would have exposed.

Don't publish your protection target, your history, or a will that names your ward while the Katana holder is still alive. Grace's public history of protecting Heidi, Erin and Alice made her the obvious Night 4 target, and her death removed the only protection on the Scout. Keep wards private and announce only a stopped attack, which is the one result that helps the Village.

Compare a Scout's group read with the visits you can confirm. A Scout result that says two players who visited each other are in separate groups means someone was role-blocked, or the Scout is lying. Ask the Scout to name the visits behind a group before anyone is hanged on it. Alice's groups put me in the Katana holder's group, and I hanged on that, but the group came from a visit nobody named.

The Yakuza Grunt cover ('Village, no night role' or 'Grunt, no night action') survived because it was never tested. The team that survived mostly denied visits, backed the Coroner's exams, and voted with the Village on the hang that was actually Village. Keep your story to a single plain sentence, and keep voting with the majority on hangs you can't avoid.

tips_feedback.tip: Treat a lone visitor to a Katana victim as near-proof only when a second source corroborates it.
tips_feedback.why: It stopped me from hanging on Alice's Night 3 group alone, which would have hit a Village player. But I still hanged Bob on a Scout group read that no one could confirm, so the tip was only half followed.

tips_feedback.tip: Before voting Guilty, name a concrete mechanical break.
tips_feedback.why: No real break existed on Bob or Erin by the end. The Village's stated breaks were Scout groups and Coroner exams that were partly false, so the hunt for a break became a hang on a Village player (Bob) and an exposed lie. The tip assumes breaks are verifiable, and this game had mostly unverifiable claims.

tips_feedback.tip: Answer a direct question about your night action in one plain sentence the first time it is asked.
tips_feedback.why: Frank's repeated dodges about Night 1 were a real suspicion, and Frank was in fact the Yakuza Grunt. The Village's pressure on that dodge is part of why he was hanged.

tips_feedback.tip: Only Mayor, Vulture and Hitman are Unique, so both claimants of any other role can be real.
tips_feedback.why: The tip is correct as a rule, but it was misapplied here. Only one Coroner and one Scout existed, and both claimants were in fact Roleplayers, so duplicate claims were not the issue. The tip also said to test claimants rather than hang on a clash, which I did, but it was no help when both checks were false.

For tips_feedback I'm sorting through which tips helped, hurt, or were simply wrong given this game's roster — noting the Katana-targeting tip helped, the "lone visitor as proof" tip hurt the Village's case against Bob, the "firm exact-role claim is a sure guess" tip was wrong since there was no Ritualist, the Medic's guarding choice arguably hurt by missing Heidi, and the "Vanilla/Grunt rarely in game" tip was flatly wrong since two Grunts existed. I'm leaving reason and feedback short/empty and keeping the notepad blank before finalizing the call.

summary:
The Yakuza (Carol and Frank, both Grunts) won even though Frank publicly claimed Grunt, a Yakuza-only role, on Day 2 and was hanged on Day 3. Three things decided the game.

1. **The Village lost its only reliable investigator early.** Heidi claimed Sheriff on Day 2, and Grace (Medic) protected Erin instead of her on Night 2. Heidi died after getting an Evil result on Frank, and her will didn't mention her Night 2 target, so the result was lost.

2. **Three of the Village were Roleplayers: Alice (believed Scout), Dave (Profiler) and Erin (Coroner).** All their results were random, and the town treated them as mechanical proof.
   - Erin's random "Frank was a Hitman" made people doubt a correct hang.
   - Alice's random visit groups were used to hang Bob (the real Vigilante) on Day 4 and Erin on Day 5. Both were Village.
   - Alice's results could not all be true. Her Night 2 claim of only 2 visit groups clashed with Grace's claimed visit to Erin. Her Night 4 claim that she and Grace were in separate groups clashed with Grace's will, which said Grace protected Alice that night. Nobody followed these clashes up, except Erin, too late.

3. **Carol played a clean low-profile game.** She claimed "Village, no night role" and was never made to name a role. She voted Guilty on her doomed teammate. She killed the claimed Sheriff, and after her attack on Alice failed she killed the protector (Grace). At 3 players she sided with Alice's false case to hang Erin, then killed Alice on Night 5.

Bob made it worse for the Village. He refused to name his role until he was on trial and never fired a shot, not even at the self-confessed Grunt.

lessons.tip: In hand-picked setups, assume Roleplayers may be in the game. Before using an investigative result to hang someone, check whether it is even possible given the visits other players have claimed. If an investigator's results contradict known facts or other claims, treat that investigator as possibly a Roleplayer, not as proof against whoever their elimination leaves.
lessons.evidence: Alice's Scout results were random. On Night 2 she reported only 2 groups, but Carol->Heidi, Grace->Erin and Heidi->Frank make at least 4 groups. On Night 4 she put herself and Grace in separate groups although Grace's will says Grace protected her. Her 'elimination' still got Bob (Vigilante) hanged on Day 4 and Erin hanged on Day 5, which lost the game.

tips_feedback.tip: After a failed attack, kill or block the likely protector rather than retrying blindly.
tips_feedback.why: After her Night 3 attack on Alice was stopped and Grace's protection became public, Carol killed Grace on Night 4. This removed the Village's only protector.

tips_feedback.tip: Guard the likeliest Katana targets and never announce your ward... Don't die holding tokens.
tips_feedback.why: Grace didn't follow this. She guarded Erin rather than Heidi, the claimed Sheriff, on Night 2, so Heidi died. Her Night 3 save on Alice worked, but she died on Night 4 with 2 unused tokens.

tips_feedback.tip: Before each night, write your planned target in your will, with what each possible result would mean.
tips_feedback.why: Heidi didn't follow this. She died with an Evil result on Frank, and her will never named her Night 2 target, so the town lost a confirmed read.

issues.description: Frank, a Yakuza Grunt, publicly claimed 'Grunt' (a Yakuza role) on Day 2 and kept that claim through his trial and in his last will. The Yakuza night chat had planned a 'Grunt cover' ('we each say we have no night action'), which suggests the player misunderstood what a cover claim is. Carol, on the same plan, claimed 'Village, no night role' instead.

The Village didn't treat Frank's Grunt claim as a confession. Heidi, Bob, Erin and Grace called it only 'Yakuza-side' and asked him for 'one concrete Night 1 detail'. Nobody nominated him on Day 2, though that day ran its full 8 rounds of near-identical messages. After Erin's random Roleplayer-Coroner result said 'Hitman', Erin concluded Frank 'was not Yakuza', trusting an unverified exam over his own role admission.

Factual slips in reasoning: on Day 5 Erin named Frank as a possible Night 3 Katana holder, but he had been hanged on Day 3. On Day 4 Bob said the Night 3 holder could be Alice, the player who was attacked that night.

Structured-output friction: Heidi's first StructuredOutput call (one JSON string with extra fields) was rejected, and Grace's call with a nested raw string failed to parse. Both worked only when each field was passed separately.
Grace reported that the turn schema has no field for a trial vote during discussion turns, so players may not know how or when their trial vote is taken.
Setup logged '[ERROR tips_stale]': every player was given a tips file last checked against an older version of the rules, so some tips may no longer hold.

The Night 4 action log reads 'Carol (Grunt): target Grace', but on other nights it says 'no role action', and Grunt has no night action. The Katana target seems to have been logged as a role target. It didn't change the result: only one visit, Carol to Grace, was recorded.

Players reported that the turn schema has no field for a role claim; the moderator records claims as '[Claim]' tags. Players used the free-text claim field inconsistently: Carol's 'Village, no night role' was vague enough that others had to ask her to name a specific role.
